item.text: The root cause is in the auth-side status refresh: it recomputes both fields from the current tunnel list, so an empty list produces a zero heartbeat and deleting the newest tunnel selects an older heartbeat. I’m checking how auth reads and writes RemoteClusters, plus the cache and backend conventions, before changing that flow.

item.text: The package tests pass. I’m tightening the update path so tunnel upserts persist the heartbeat immediately; otherwise a connection created and deleted before the next RemoteCluster read could still lose its last heartbeat. I’m also covering the cluster scoped and global bulk delete methods.

item.text:
Implemented persistent RemoteCluster status and heartbeat updates. Tunnel upserts now record the latest heartbeat; deletes refresh status while retaining the highest recorded heartbeat. With no connections, clusters are marked Offline without clearing that heartbeat.

Added `Presence.UpdateRemoteCluster` with expiry and resource ID preservation, plus the authenticated API and client method required by the interface.

**Verification:** Local presence, cache, and services tests passed. Filtered auth tunnel and RemoteCluster CRUD tests passed. Full auth runs hit `PasswordSuite.TestTiming` twice, exceeding its 10% timing threshold by 10.79% and 12.05%.
